newsitem.title: ITALY: Telecom Italia defends cordless phone plan.
newsitem.headline: Telecom Italia defends cordless phone plan.

text.p: Italy's state-controlled fixed-line telecoms operator Telecom Italia said its plan to launch a supercordless DECT phone was an evolution of its fixed line business in offering consumers new innovative services.

Telecom Italia's managing director Francesco Chirichigno was defending the group's plan to launch a cordless phone system using the Digital European Cordless Telephony (DECT) standard in an interview with Italy's daily La Stampa newspaper.

The company's announcement of its plans in October to launch a DECT service sparked controversy when Italy's ani-trust authority chairman Giuliano Amato said if it went ahead it would be taking advantage of Telecom Italia's dominant position in the fixed-line market and compete with mobile phone operators.
"For us DECT is an evolution of the fixed line market, and this technology will allow the possibility of offering innovative services to consumers," Chirichigno said.

He added that the DECT service was part of a two-year strategic plan that was approved by the Italian Post Ministry last year. He hopes that the green light will be given for his company and others to operate this system.

Telecom Italia's sister company, the mobile operator Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM), is also seeking authorisation to offer a DECT cordless phone service, while Italy's second mobile phone group Omnitel has asked for authorisation to experiment with DECT technology.
The Italian Post Ministry has not yet defined the full authorisation rules for cordless phones.

Telecom Italia plans to invest 1.8 trillion lire and to involve 6,500 employees in the launch of its DECT system, called Fido, which would allow telecom users take their telephones with them when they leave home.

Asked whether he would step down when Telecom Italia is merged with telecoms holding group STET and then fully privatised, like STET's managing director Ernesto Pascale has promised, Chirichigno said it was up to the group's shareholders.
STET is currently majority owned by the Italian Treasury, while STET itself has majority shareholdings in both Telecom Italia and TIM.
